Start here: Instructors

Source: vignettes/articles/for-instructors.Rmd
for-instructors.Rmd

mirtverse gives you a complete, free set of materials for a course on item response theory: A book, ten interactive labs, a 12-week course map, a glossary and a cheat sheet. Everything is open, editable and runs on student laptops.

Your path in three steps

1. See how the pieces fit a semester. The course map ties each week to a book chapter, a lab and a reading, and the sample syllabus (Word) turns it into a document you can edit and hand out.

2. Try a lab the way your students will. Each lab is a realistic case, such as advising a certification board or investigating a fairness complaint, with live mirt models and decisions to defend:

library(mirtverse)
list_labs()                 # the ten labs
run_lab("fairness")         # Lab 3: Is the test fair?

The Teaching labs article has the learning goals, timing, discussion prompts and an answer key for each lab.

3. Make it yours. Build a lab on your own data, swap the dataset in a built-in lab, or copy a book chapter to edit:

new_course("irt-fall-2027")                    # a course folder
new_lab("my-lab", data = mydata, course = "irt-fall-2027")
check_material("irt-fall-2027")                # checks every lab before class does

See The instructor toolkit. If you use Claude or an OpenAI assistant, the MCP server lets it revise and adapt these materials for you.

Also for your course

  • The book, also as PDF and EPUB, with its own DOI (10.5281/zenodo.23885605).
  • AI in measurement: Four labs and six chapters on AI for a later module, and a one-day workshop kit.
  • Glossary and cheat sheet to hand out.

Adopting it for a course?

Adopt mirtverse for your course has a sample syllabus to edit (Word and PDF), a setup checklist, and a two-minute form to tell us about your course. Hearing which courses use the materials shapes what comes next.
